- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (≤ 0.33) in recent days; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downward trends.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a steep drop, reduce forecast peak by 10–15% to account for overreaction.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope downward by 2–5% to reflect mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, cap forecast decline in later days to avoid premature reversal.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 5+ days, apply a 5–10% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in rebound.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67); use smoother, more conservative trajectories.
